Worktree path is already fast; env reuse and snapshot capture are the missing 90%.

checked.why_killer: Best-of-5 or an eight-teammate fan-out starts in seconds rather than waiting on five `npm install`s, which is what makes parallelism cheap enough to use by default. Competitors moved this bar in August; bog's parallel-worktree and sandbox factory paths are where it plugs in, and the daemon benefits on every trigger.

checked.evidence: none found after grepping 'stream-json|codex exec|claude -p|HarnessSubAgent|external harness|multi.harness' in libs — only bog's own stream-json emitter (libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/json_output.py:20-25, main.py:658, non_interactive.py:167); libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/subagents.py:32-188 (subagents are markdown-spec bog agents; bundled_agents/{go,node,python,rust}); libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/hook_middleware.py / hook_decisions.py (decisions enforced only on bog's own tool path)
checked.delta: SDK `HarnessSubAgentBackend` launching `claude -p --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json`, `codex exec --json`, and grok headless, with per-harness event adapters to a common ToolCallEvent; governance by installing a bog hook into the child harness's own hook mechanism (Claude Code/Cursor hook files are already understood by hook_decisions.py) that calls back a `bog-agents hook-proxy` over a local socket so Expert Mode / SafeTools / DLP / classify_git_command decide each external tool call (stream-json alone cannot veto mid-flight); usage events -> CostLedger.tracker_for(label); result folded into TeamReport + EvidenceBundle; selectable per workflow phase (`harness: claude|codex|bog`). checked.why_killer: A team keeps the harness each developer already loves while security gets one policy engine, one audit trail and one cost cap across all of them — the value Warp charges enterprises for, delivered as a self-hosted Python package. Grok Build's headless output is wire-compatible with Anthropic stream-json (per the July review), so two of three harnesses share one adapter.

checked.competitor: Cursor Bugbot June update: /review pre-push, diff dedupe, incremental review, effort levels (Jun 10)
checked.why_killer: A developer who ran the review locally is not charged and not nagged again when the same diff lands in the PR, and follow-up pushes get feedback only on the new hunks. v1 #3 shipped self-review with five lenses; Bugbot moved the bar to incremental + deduped + effort-graded, all of which are cheap on top of bog's existing controller and rubric grader.
